reviews.text: Absolutely at a loss for words how they know my dog is on his death bed and tell me to get the wellness care because I can cancel it after putting him down just to turn around and be told I’m locked into a year contract days after. They pull on your heart strings while all saying the same script “oh I’m sorry for your loss” then in the same breath ask for money. I’m utter disgusted with this place

This is the worst Banfield in town. They are completely unhelpful when it comes to follow ups, dealing with med refills will take hours, and they will tell you one thing on the phone and then you show up and they tell you that info was wrong. Take yourself to the Shea location.

I brought in a sick kitten to this veterinary clinic back in May. He was not eating or drinking, and he had difficulty breathing. I dropped him off, and when I returned, the veterinarian told me he was going to die because I was neglectful in bottle-feeding him, and he had asphyxiated. Keep in mind...the kitten was not bottle-fed. He was old enough to eat wet food, and he hadn't been in my care that long. They also tried charging me 60 bucks just to put a red light on the kitten to check for ringworm...I could buy a red light for five bucks and do it myself. Long story short, they wanted me to euthanize the kitten for 180 dollars!! I went home crying with the kitten, and the next day I took him to a different vet, where they prescribed him some medicine to treat the ringworm and medicine to help with the mucus in his airway. They also gave me an appetite stimulant for his lack of appetite. This veterinarian told me the kitten was nowhere near dying and he would improve with medication. The kitten is now thriving in his new home, and I attached some pictures below! (: I will never visit this clinic again. And I would highly recommend seeking a different opinion if you ever visit Banfield Pet Hospital.

Brought my mother's dog, Itty-Bitty, in for a 10:15 AM drop-off appointment for vaccine updates and a nail trim/dremel. No one came to the front desk to check her in for about 10 minutes. When I called around noon for an update, I was told they were understaffed and the earliest she'd be ready was 1:30 PM — then 10 minutes later I got a call saying she was already ready. The inconsistency didn't inspire confidence.

Paid $228.85 for the visit, but the account statement shows nothing beyond the billing total — no itemized breakdown, no exam notes, no summary of what was actually done. The only thing I received was a rabies certificate. I have no way to confirm the nail trim and dremel I paid for were even completed.

They already have their money, but getting an actual response has been another story. I've reached out through Banfield Cares and gotten nothing but automated acknowledgments — first promising a reply in two business days, then quietly extended to three-to-five, with no substance in between. If you want documentation of what was actually done for your pet, don't count on getting it easily.

Given the lack of transparency and unresponsiveness, this was my first and last visit to Banfield.

As always, the clinician who met with me was pleasant, professional and volunteered sound information about my pet, preventive care and services offered.  When my dog was taken back to the vet area for service, they finished very quickly, leaving me with hardly a wait time.  It was excellent as always and I really wanted to share kudos on line for their consistent excellent pet care and customer service.

I’m really frustrated with my experience at Banfield Pet Hospital (Biltmore Phoenix). I brought my dog in because of a serious stomach issue and diphtheria for few days, and while I was in the room with the vet, we specifically agreed to run a fecal test to help figure out what’s going on. It’s was even in the notes, when I called in and speak with another doctor.
I left my dog there for the entire day, expecting answers. Two days later, I called to get the test results—only to be told that the test was never even done.
On top of that, I was still charged around $500 for completely different test results not related to the stomach issue, and when I tried to get clarification, no one at the clinic seemed to know anything about my dog or the situation.
When  I look on visit summary on my Banfield  app, it’s shows I brought dog for eye/year/nose check up.
That’s is not true!
What’s the point of paying for a premium Plus membership if agreed-upon care isn’t followed through and communication is this poor? This experience has been incredibly disappointing and concerning.

I also have him on the wellness plan which helped payed for the visit, the urinalysis, X-rays and blood work. Outstanding customer service, thanks!

I honestly can’t believe what just happened. I brought my dog in for a simple procedure, and they dropped him off the table. You read that right. They literally dropped my dog. Now he can’t even put pressure on his paw — he’s limping, whimpering, and clearly in pain. Watching him try to walk breaks my heart.

When I reached out to them through the “wellness program” chat (which, by the way, I pay $80 a month for), their response wasn’t an apology or an offer to help. Instead, they told me to take him to another animal hospital — one that’s not even covered under their plan. So now I’m supposed to pay another vet out of pocket to fix what they caused?

I trusted this clinic with my dog’s care, and they completely let me down. No compassion, no responsibility, just a “not our problem” attitude. My dog deserves better — every pet does. I wouldn’t recommend this place to anyone who actually cares about their animal

We've taken in both of our dogs for issues in which we barely spoke to a vet. All communication was done via their staff. Most recently, we took our female dog in for a cough and sneezing and its been weeks to trying to determine what's wrong with her with us pushing for tests to be done because the staff recommended we just "monitor her." At the last visit, we did some respiratory tests and were told we'd have results in 3-4 days. We have been following up for TWO WEEKS and were continuously told that the lab was taking a long time to find out that the Banfield team did not submit the correct paperwork so the lab didn't perform any testing at all. This was after they told us they were calling the lab everytime we called to ask for results, which means they never did because the lab would have told them they had a paperwork issue. I cannot say anything positive about this location.

I brought my dog Max to Banfield Pet Hospital – Biltmore twice in the last month, and both experiences were unacceptable. Despite spending over $500, I received no clear diagnosis for Max’s worsening coughing and sneezing. Instead, I was met with repeated upselling of high-cost services that felt unrelated to his condition. Dr. Dana Robinson provided no clarity, and Practice Manager Jolene Myers was dismissive and unprofessional when I asked for help understanding my pet’s discharge papers — which were never explained to me at any point.

After being told to "wait a minute," I was left alone in the front lobby for over 40 minutes. While waiting, I observed unsecured client documents at the front desk with names, addresses, phone numbers, pet names, and prescription information in plain view — a serious breach of privacy I’ve reported to federal regulators.

Rather than offering support, Banfield staff escalated the matter by calling the police and falsely claiming I was irate. I have video proof that I remained calm throughout the encounter. I have since filed formal complaints with the Arizona Attorney General, HHS Office for Civil Rights, Federal Trade Commission, and the Arizona State Veterinary Board.

Additionally, Banfield advertises a “First Visit Free” promotion, which they failed to honor for Max’s first visit — a practice now under investigation for false advertising.

This review is not written lightly. I expected responsible, compassionate care. Instead, I encountered indifference, disrespect, and retaliation. I urge other pet owners to be cautious before trusting this location with their pets' health.

When looking upon the paper work of the check up they only had reported that she had received her vaccines, but when we asked about getting a doctors note of the incident of the bloody ear they got super defensive and told us that they couldn’t have possibly caused that bodily harm to our pet.
